clue.text: We run by building in Berkshire

indicators.note: building means putting together, so these letters are assembled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of jogging past some building in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges WE RUN BY into the town's name; 'in Berkshire' is the definition, a place found in that English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Newbury is a market town in the English county of Berkshire, famous for its racecourse.

clue.text: It's unsightly to look resentful

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
sore means aggrieved or resentful

explanation.surface: Something ugly makes you look resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsightly thing is a blot on the landscape, an ugly sight that offends the viewer.

clue.text: Sudden increase in the openings of bars under local government encouragement

indicators.note: openings are beginnings, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: More bars open thanks to council encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulge is a temporary swelling in numbers, as in a baby bulge.

clue.text: Bishop accepts blame surprisingly for Rose

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters of the following word appear in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A bishop surprisingly takes the blame over a rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' with a capital looks like a name or a verb; it is the climbing flower. 'surprisingly' makes AMBLE, and RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's style.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a climbing rose with long trailing stems.

clue.text: Idler putting newspaper inside towel

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: a towel is used to dry, so it is a drier
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone wraps a newspaper inside a towel.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is an aimless person without steady work, a loafer.

clue.text: Angular figures seen by house doctor in Rhode Island

indicators.note: in places the pieces within the state abbreviation

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Geometric shapes are spotted near a doctor's surgery in Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhombi, plural of rhombus, are four-sided figures with equal sides and slanted angles.

clue.text: Lie when expressing surprise, say, about educational establishment getting in meat

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so this combination goes inside the next word's synonym

parts.note: meat in the old sense means food generally

indicators.note: about means around, so the exclamation wraps the college

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of surprise, given as an example
LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A surprised cry about a college serving meat is untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meat' in its old sense means any food, as in 'meat and drink'. 'about' makes ALSEH, which 'getting in' sets inside the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is an untrue statement, so it is a synonym for a lie.

clue.text: Set aside final ace and prepare to do battle with a pair of kings

indicators.note: final means the last letter of the following word

parts.note: to arm is to equip for fighting
R (rex) and K are both abbreviations for king

explanation.surface: A card player holds the last ace and two kings, ready for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to reserve or set them apart for a purpose.

clue.text: He always takes her part!

parts.note: in a British Christmas pantomime the comic female lead is traditionally played by a man, so he always takes her role

explanation.surface: A loyal man always sides with his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes her part' reads as standing up for her, but it means playing her role on stage; British pantomime is a Christmas family show with stock characters.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock comic older woman of British pantomime is always played by a male actor in drag.

clue.text: See 27
Songster of field and frolic

parts.note: a meadow is a grassy field
a lark is a bit of fun or a frolic

explanation.surface: A singer is made of open fields and carefree fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadowlark is an American songbird, and a songster is any singing bird.

clue.text: Weary with a line from "The North Wind"

parts.note: to bore someone is to weary them

explanation.surface: A tired reader quotes a line from a work called The North Wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Boreas was the Greek god of the north wind, and the adjective derived from him means northern.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective boreal derives from Boreas, the Greek north wind, so it means belonging to the northern regions.

clue.text: Competent scholar embraced by non-drinker takes cover

indicators.note: embraced by means held within, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a non-drinker
able means competent
MA, Master of Arts, denotes a scholar

explanation.surface: A capable academic hugged by a teetotaller finds shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A table mat is a protective pad placed on a table to cover its surface.

clue.text: Said to be genially drunk on a wee whisky, a piece of exaggeration

indicators.note: said signals the letters come from how the words are spoken

parts.words: genially drunk on a wee whisky
parts.note: mellow means genially tipsy, a dram is a small whisky, and a stays as a

explanation.surface: A tipsy man after a small Scotch tells an overblown story.
explanation.walkthrough: MELLOW + DRAM + A, spoken quickly, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational, overdone play or piece of overacting.

clue.text: Crush gets too much for wife at steering wheel

parts.note: over means excessive, as in overpaid
a ship's helm is its wheel or tiller

explanation.surface: A husband feels it is too much having his wife at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm is to crush or defeat utterly with superior force.

clue.text: Woody's a lad accepting return of heartless kiss

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the lad holds the other piece

parts.note: a boy is a lad

indicators.note: return means going back, so the letters are read backwards
heartless removes the middle of the word, keeping its outer letters

explanation.surface: A lad called Woody receives a returned kiss without passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woody's' is read as 'Woody is', not a possessive; 'heartless' leaves two letters, and 'return of' turns them before 'accepting' takes them in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosky is a literary word meaning wooded or covered with bushes.

clue.text: Like the garden, all awry

parts.note: as means like
Kew Gardens, in London, is the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: Like a neglected garden, everything is crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW Gardens is the famous botanic garden in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew means crooked or out of line, the same as awry.

clue.text: Soak in the Spanish architectural feature

parts.note: to steep is to soak in liquid
the setter meant the definite article in a foreign language; LE is French for the

explanation.surface: A tourist soaks up the sights of a Spanish building.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer needs LE, which is French for 'the'; the Spanish article is EL, so 'Spanish' is the setter's slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a church tower with a spire, a classic architectural feature.

clue.text: Approaching a denouement after one politician is threatening

indicators.note: after places the ending piece behind the first two

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
a denouement is the ending of a story

explanation.surface: A politician faces a climax that is looming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impending is about to happen, often ominously, so it is menacing.

clue.text: Dub with style

definitions.meaning: to dub is to give a name or title to
en- plus title, to give a style or title to someone

explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to name or confer a title, as a monarch dubs a knight.

clue.text: Actor Paul keeps the Sabbath; he helps to spread the word

definitions.text: he helps to spread the word

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so one piece goes inside the surname

parts.note: Paul Newman was an American film actor
S is an abbreviation for Sabbath

explanation.surface: An actor observes the Sabbath and spreads the gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsman is a reporter or journalist, someone whose work spreads news.

clue.text: Sings of the Yorkshire flowers

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
flowers here are things that flow, so streams or rills

explanation.surface: Someone sings about Yorkshire flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' is not blooms but things that flow: rills are small streams.
explanation.definitionFit: To trill is to sing with a quavering warble, as birds do.

clue.text: Student taken in by unfamiliar expression from America

parts.note: new means unfamiliar

indicators.note: taken in by means contained within, so the student goes inside

parts.note: a word is an expression
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student is fooled by a strange American phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Americas are called the New World, as opposed to Europe's Old World.

clue.text: Cast from the seat of kings, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the letters come from how a word is spoken

parts.note: a throne is a monarch's seat

explanation.surface: A king is ousted from his throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown is the past participle of throw, which means cast or hurled.

clue.text: Game not started by a back

indicators.note: not started means without its first letter

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A game left unfinished by a sports back.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow raised strip, like the backbone of an animal or a roof's top.

clue.text: Nonchalantly dispel time restriction

indicators.note: nonchalantly suggests carelessly, so the letters are scattered loosely

explanation.surface: Casually wave away a time limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed limit is a legal restriction on how fast vehicles may travel.

clue.text: Mum's gong for developing muscles

parts.note: mum means silent, and so does dumb; the 's is a link
a gong is a kind of bell

explanation.surface: Mother's medal for building up her muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother but means silent; 'gong' is British slang for a medal but here is the bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbbell is a short bar with weights, used in exercises that build muscle.

clue.text: From maybe a mishap, emerges radiant

indicators.note: from signals that the answer is taken out of the following run of words

explanation.surface: Someone comes out of an accident smiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Beamish, coined by Lewis Carroll, means beaming with happiness, so radiant.

clue.text: Estate workers, including gardeners, finally dive into the river

indicators.note: dive into means plunge inside, so this goes within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a British river

indicators.note: including means holding within

parts.note: men are workers

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of gardeners

explanation.surface: Estate staff, gardeners last, plunge into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland. 'including' makes MESN, and 'dive into' sets it in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held by a lord, an estate.
